_about: Always-flag interaction pairs from the ONC high-priority drug-drug interaction list (Phansalkar 2012, Table 2). Owner: B. Checked against the paper on 2026-10-28 (see docs/DATA_SOURCES.md, verification log). The paper defines these as pairs that should not be prescribed together and says its class lists are not complete; summaries are in our own words and add no mechanism or symptom the paper does not state.

source.title: High-priority drug-drug interactions for use in electronic health records
source.citation: Phansalkar S, et al. J Am Med Inform Assoc. 2012;19(5):735-743. doi:10.1136/amiajnl-2011-000612

rules.summary: Simvastatin or lovastatin with this medicine (a strong CYP3A4 blocker) is on an expert list of drug pairs that should not be prescribed together.
Tizanidine with this medicine (a CYP1A2 blocker) is on an expert list of drug pairs that should not be prescribed together.
An MAO inhibitor antidepressant with an amphetamine-like medicine is on an expert list of drug pairs that should not be prescribed together.
An MAO inhibitor with this serotonin-acting antidepressant is on an expert list of drug pairs that should not be prescribed together.
An MAO inhibitor with this opioid-type medicine is on an expert list of drug pairs that should not be prescribed together.
Atazanavir with a stomach-acid reducer (proton pump inhibitor) is on an expert list of drug pairs that should not be prescribed together.
Ramelteon with fluvoxamine is on an expert list of drug pairs that should not be prescribed together.
